newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fortis confirms talks on ASLK stake rise.
newsitem.headline: Fortis confirms talks on ASLK stake rise.

text.p: Dutch-Belgian financial group Fortis confirmed on Wednesday it was in talks with a Belgian government committee on upping its stake in state-owned bank ASLK.
ASLK was partially privatised just over three years ago with the sale of 49.9 percent stake in the bank to Fortis.
Fortis hopes the Belgian government will excercise a put option it holds on 9.8 percent of the ASLK shares and sell a further 15 percent.
"We are in talks," Fortis spokesman Corneel Maes said. "But, I'm not saying we are negotiating," he added.
Last November Fortis co-chairman Maurice Lippens said that Fortis expected the Belgian government to reduce its stake in ASLK in 1997.
Maes said Fortis was in talks with the Abraham committee, which is handling the further privatisation of ASLK.
Fortis is also in talks with the the government-linked venture capital unit which is also involved in the sell-off.
